examples.before:
.troupe/troupe.yml:
# main config
model: opus  # default model
retries: 2
agents:
  coder: file:agents/coder.yaml

examples.input: edit `.troupe/troupe.yml` by hand to `model: sonnet  # default model`, then `config get model`
edit `.troupe/agents/coder.yaml` by hand from `temperature: 0.2` to `temperature: 0.7`, then `config get agents.coder.temperature`
`config history` after those two hand edits and gets

results.1: all three arms: exit 0; 4 import entries (model opus, retries 2, agents.coder.temperature 0.2, agents.coder.role coder), then seq 5 `set model opus -> sonnet` and seq 6 `set agents.coder.temperature 0.2 -> 0.7`, both `"via": "file"` and sharing one change id
results.2: all three arms: exit 0; same six entries, including seq 5 `set model opus -> sonnet` and seq 6 `set agents.coder.temperature 0.2 -> 0.7`, both `"via": "file"`

results.1:
all three arms: exit 0, prints:
model: sonnet
retries: 2
agents:
  coder:
    temperature: 0.7
    role: coder
results.2: all three arms: exit 0, same output

context.in_practice: All six arms gave the same results, apart from timestamps and change ids. On both routes, `config get` returned the hand-edited values, and history recorded each hand edit as a `via: file` change. This test doesn't show which command wrote those history entries. No config file was changed by any troupe command.
context.stakes: After someone edits `.troupe/troupe.yml` or an agent file by hand, the question is whether `config get` returns the edited value or a stale one, and whether the edit gets recorded in history. In this test, both routes behaved the same way.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 deliberately reconciles hand edits on `get`, the same way `show` does. Route 2 never considered the question but behaved the same way here, so this test shows no difference between them.

plan_why: Files are edited by hand after the first import, then `get` runs before any `show`. The examples show whether `get` returns the hand-edited values from the main file and from an included file, whether `history` then has `set` events (via file, unknown actor) for those edits, and whether a later `show` agrees with what `get` printed.
